# MethodCache: instructions for coding agents

Copy this file into your project as agent instructions, for example as `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, a Cursor
rule, a Claude Code skill or a section of `AGENTS.md`. It tells a coding agent how to add caching with MethodCache
correctly. Full docs: https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/README.md

## Adding caching to a service

1. The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. Nothing else is needed
   for in-memory caching.
2. Put `[Cache]` on the **interface** method, never on the class. Put `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = [...])]` on the
   interface methods that change the data. Don't change the implementation.
3. Register services as usual, then call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` **after** them.

```cs
public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

## Rules

- Only interface methods that return a value can be cached: sync, `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`. Return a list, never
  a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`.
- Callers must use the interface. Calling the method from inside the class, or resolving the class itself, bypasses
  the cache.
- Keys are generated from the method and its arguments; don't write keys for `[Cache]` methods. A `CancellationToken`
  is not part of the key. Every value that changes the result must be a parameter.
- Tags take templates with a **parameter name** only: `"product:{id}"`. `"{product.Id}"` is not a template, stays
  literal and gives warning MCG015; add an `id` parameter instead. Use the same tags on the cached method and on its `[CacheInvalidate]`.
- Put ids (`int`, `Guid`) in tag templates, not free text from users: tags are plain text, so `"1:orders"` in
  `"user:{id}"` equals `"user:{id}:orders"` for id 1. Never pass passwords or tokens as arguments of cached methods.
- Durations are `TimeSpan` strings: `Duration = "00:10:00"`. Other settings: `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`,
  `FailSafe` (or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout`, `Version`, `Tags`, and a group name as the first argument.
- Cached objects are shared between callers: return immutable types such as records.
- For a type with only private state used as an argument or inside one (a property, a list element), implement
  `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- For a client from a NuGet package with an interface, use
  `[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(IClient), nameof(IClient.Method), Duration = "...")]` instead of a wrapper.
- Without an attribute, use `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync(key, factory, o => o.WithDuration(...))` with an explicit,
  prefixed key such as `$"order:{id}"`.
- Fix every `MC` and `MCG` build diagnostic; each links to its explanation, and many have a code fix.
- In tests, register `NoOpCacheManager` (namespace `MethodCache.Extensibility`) after `AddMethodCache()` to turn
  caching off.

## Namespaces

- `MethodCache`: `[Cache]`, `[CacheInvalidate]`, `[CacheInterface]`, `ICacheManager`, `ICacheAdministrator`,
  `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`, `MethodCacheKeys`, `MethodCacheMemoryOptions`, `Any<T>`, `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- `MethodCache.Extensibility`: `ISerializer`, `JsonCacheSerializer`, `ICacheKeyGenerator`, `JsonKeyGenerator`,
  `NoOpCacheManager`.
- `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`: `AddMethodCache`, `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration`,
  `AddMethodCacheRedis` (package `MethodCache.Redis`), `AddMethodCacheSqlServer` (package `MethodCache.SqlServer`).

Custom distributed method-result caches must implement `MethodCache.Extensibility.IAtomicInvalidationStore`,
including backend-atomic maximum timestamps and retention preservation. A plain `IDistributedCache` is
rejected when the host starts (`ValidateOnStart`), or without a generic host when the method cache manager is
resolved. Redis and SQL Server supply this contract.

`AddHttpCaching()` disables automatic cookies on the named client’s `SocketsHttpHandler` or `HttpClientHandler` after handler configuration. Send caller cookies explicitly before the cache handler. Unknown transports bypass caching with a warning unless `AllowUnverifiedTransport` is enabled after verifying that the entire transport has no automatic cookies or hidden caller identity.

For direct invalidation or administration of versioned fluent entries, use `CacheManagerExtensions.GetCacheKey(logicalKey, version)`. Treat the returned identity as opaque; callback `CacheContext.Key` remains the logical key.

`AddHttpCaching()` runs the cache after all additional handlers, so injected caller identity and rewritten requests are visible before lookup. Delegating handlers inside the primary transport, or below a directly constructed cache handler, are unverified and bypass caching unless the entire chain is explicitly trusted.

Unversioned fluent keys that begin with NUL are escaped too. Use `CacheManagerExtensions.GetCacheKey(logicalKey)` for direct invalidation or administration of those entries, just as you use the overload with a version for versioned entries.

# Getting started

MethodCache is not on nuget.org yet. Until it is, reference the projects from this repository (the
[demo's project file](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo/MethodCache.Demo.csproj) shows how). Once published:

```bash
dotnet add package MethodCache
```

The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. It supports .NET 8, 9 and 10.

## 1. Start from a service

A typical service talks to a database on every call:

```cs
public sealed class ProductService(Database db)
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

## 2. Put the attributes on its interface

`[Cache]` goes on interface methods that return data, `[CacheInvalidate]` on the methods that change it. The
implementation doesn't change:

```cs
public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

- `GetAsync(42)` is stored for ten minutes under a key built from the method and its argument
  (`...IProductService.GetAsync:42`). The `CancellationToken` is not part of the key.
- `"product:{id}"` is a tag template: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `product:42`.
- `UpdateAsync(42, ...)` removes every entry tagged `products` or `product:42` once it has completed.

The attributes must be on the interface. On a class they do nothing, and the analyzer reports
[MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) with a code fix that moves them.

## 3. Register it

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

`AddMethodCache()` wraps every registered interface that has cached methods in its generated decorator and keeps the
lifetime you chose. Call it after your own registrations: a service registered later is not cached. If you don't
register an implementation at all, `AddMethodCache()` registers it as a singleton when it lives in the same project as
the interface.

Generic interfaces work the same way: `IRepository<User>` is cached for every closed type a class in your project
implements, such as `UserRepository : IRepository<User>`. An open generic registration such as
`AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), typeof(Repository<>))` is not cached; register the closed types instead.

## What can be cached

```cs
[Cache] Product Get(int id);                          // synchronous
[Cache] Task<Product> GetAsync(int id);               // Task<T>
[Cache] ValueTask<Product> GetFastAsync(int id);      // ValueTask<T>
[Cache] Task<Product?> FindAsync(string name);        // null results are cached too
```

- Synchronous methods, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>` can be cached. A method that returns nothing has nothing to
  cache, so `[Cache]` on it is a build error ([MCG001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg001),
  [MCG002](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg002)). So is a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`
  ([MCG014](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg014)): return a list.
- Exceptions are never cached: the next call runs the method again.
- Concurrent calls with the same arguments share one call to your method (stampede protection). A caller that cancels
  only stops its own wait.
- `null` results are cached. Turn that off with `CacheNullValues` on the [memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md), or
  per method with [conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md).
- The cached object is returned as is, not copied. Treat cached results as read-only.

## Next steps

- Choose how long entries live: [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md).
- Remove entries when data changes: [Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).
- Change durations without a redeploy: [Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md).
- Share the cache between instances: [Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md).
