<!-- source: docs/security.md -->

# Security

What each package protects against, what it leaves to you, and the tests that hold it to that.

## MethodCache (keys, tags, invalidation)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| A caller crafts an argument (`"1:orders"`, `"a)"`, a newline) so that their call gets another call's key and its cached result | Keys separate arguments unambiguously: string parts escape `\` and `:`, `null` is `\0`, records are `(a:b)` with escaped members, and hashed keys length-prefix every value and record the runtime type of values in `object`, base-class or interface slots (`1` and `1L` in an `object[]` differ). JSON and MessagePack key-provider parts and nested strings preserve exact UTF-16 code units, including lone surrogates. Recursive key generation from providers or JSON getters cannot overwrite another invocation's key arguments. Arguments whose only state is private, including fields inherited from base classes, are rejected rather than hashed as an empty object. Overloaded methods include the namespaces of their parameter types, so equally named types from different namespaces cannot share a method identity. No argument list produces another method's key or another argument list's key. Fluent versions have a separate namespace, with reserved user-key prefixes escaped, so a crafted raw key cannot reach a versioned entry. |
| An argument that is a secret ends up readable | Keys contain argument values in plain text (hashed keys are not encryption) and appear in the admin endpoints and, if you turn them on, in traces. Don't cache methods that take passwords or tokens; pass an id. |
| A tag built from user text invalidates someone else's entries | **Not prevented.** Tags are plain text: `"user:{userId}"` with the id `"1:orders"` is the same tag that `"user:{userId}:orders"` gives user 1, so invalidating one also removes the other. This only ever removes entries (they are loaded again); it never serves one caller's value to another. Use ids that can't contain your separator (`int`, `Guid`) in tag templates. |
| A load races invalidation and a newer write | Invalidated loads cannot publish over newer entries, even when custom weight calculation stalls or re-enters the cache. Existing callers may finish with their pre-invalidation result; later loads and writes retain their own entry. |
| A tag built from user text clears the whole distributed cache | L2 metadata preserves every UTF-16 code unit, including lone surrogates, so reading a tag cannot change its invalidation identity. A tag is only ever its own tag, whatever characters it holds; the internal "clear everything" marker can't be named by a tag. |
| `*` or `?` in user text widens an invalidation | `InvalidateByTagsAsync`, `InvalidateByKeysAsync` and the admin endpoints match exactly. Only `InvalidateByTagPatternAsync` reads wildcards: never build its pattern from user text. Patterns are matched without regular expressions, so a pattern can't cause catastrophic backtracking. |
| `[CacheKey(UseAsRawKey = true)]` | The argument *is* the key, unescaped, so a caller who controls it can read any other entry with that key. Use it only for keys your code builds. |

## Distributed cache (Redis, SQL Server)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| Corrupt, truncated or crafted bytes in the distributed cache | Read as a miss and loaded again: never an exception for the caller, never a `null` that wasn't stored, and lengths in the data are checked against its size before anything is allocated. |
| Stored data names a type to create (deserialization gadgets) | `JsonCacheSerializer` reads the method's declared type and ignores `$type`. `MessagePackCacheSerializer` uses the contractless resolver with `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData` and refuses typeless payloads. Keep it that way if you pass your own options. |
| Someone who can write to Redis or SQL Server | **Not prevented.** They can store any well-formed value, which every instance will serve. Custom method-result providers must implement backend-atomic invalidation stamps through `IAtomicInvalidationStore`; plain read-modify-write providers are rejected. The distributed cache is trusted: protect it like your database (authentication, TLS, network rules), and give each application its own `KeyPrefix`. Redis uses injective escaping before UTF-8 encoding, including for atomic stamps, so different UTF-16 keys cannot alias through replacement characters. SQL Server hashes exact UTF-16 cache keys so collation cannot alias distinct data or invalidation metadata keys, including NULs and trailing spaces. SQL Server also scopes backplane messages and cleanup by that exact prefix, independently of database collation. |
| Backplane messages | Carry keys and tags in lossless UTF-16 frames, so lone surrogates cannot change invalidation identity and newlines cannot forge another message type. Anyone who can publish on the channel can invalidate entries, so the same trust applies. |

## MethodCache.AspNetCore (admin endpoints)

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| An endpoint reachable without authorization | `MapMethodCacheAdmin` requires an authorization policy name, and every endpoint it maps requires that policy: anonymous callers get 401, signed-in users without it 403. A test reads the app's route table and checks every mapped endpoint, so a new endpoint without the policy fails a test. |
| A cross-site form or `fetch` without preflight calls `invalidate` with the admin's cookie | `POST invalidate` only accepts `application/json`, which a browser sends cross-site only after a CORS preflight; forms and `text/plain` get 415. The `DELETE` endpoints need a preflight too. Don't add a CORS policy that allows these routes from other origins. |
| Cached values leak through the admin API | Entries are listed with key, value type, age, time to live, tags and size, never the value. Keys contain argument values (see above), so the policy should admit only operators. |
| Bad input | A missing `key` or an out-of-range `limit` is 400, an empty or blank tag list is 400, and keys and tags are matched literally, never as patterns. |

The health check reports counts only. If you map it with a detailed response writer, put that endpoint behind
authorization too.

## MethodCache.HttpCaching

| Threat | What MethodCache does |
|---|---|
| Two users of one `HttpClient` get each other's responses (private cache, the default) | `Authorization` and `Cookie` are part of every response's key, including values that don't parse as a credential, so each caller only gets responses fetched with their own headers. `AddHttpCaching()` disables automatic cookies on known transports; explicitly supplied cookie headers isolate callers. Unknown transports bypass caching unless explicitly verified and opted in. A directly constructed cache handler also bypasses known transports with automatic cookies enabled. An empty header and no header are different callers too. Header values are individually length-framed, so a comma inside one value cannot alias two separate values. |
| A 304 changes response privacy or variant selection | Revalidated representations are checked again: `no-store`, `Vary: *` or shared-cache `private` removes previous responses. An omitted `Vary` keeps its previous value. |
| A shared cache (`IsSharedCache = true`) stores a personal response | Responses marked `private`, and responses to requests with any `Authorization` header, are not stored unless they say `public`, `s-maxage` or `must-revalidate` (RFC 9111 section 3.5). |
| Stale content bypasses required validation | Response or request `no-cache` requires successful validation even with stale-while-revalidate or stale-if-error enabled; origin failures propagate. |
| A cached response hands out a session | `Set-Cookie` is never stored. The caller the origin answered gets it, including on a `304`; nobody answered from the cache does. |
| Responses that vary by a header (tenant, language) get mixed | `Vary` and `KeyHeaders` keep one response per value. `Vary: *` is never served from the cache. |
| A write leaves another caller's stale copy, or serves one caller's copy to another after it | A successful `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` changes the publication generation for every caller. Older in-flight responses write into an obsolete namespace. Shared generation records must be retained and protected from eviction; invalidation failures propagate to the caller. |
| Two URLs share an entry | The key is the method and the full URL, with reserved characters kept escaped (`%2F`, `%3F` and `/`, `?` are different URLs). |
| Crafted entries in the distributed HTTP cache | Read as a miss, with every length checked against the data. As above, whoever can write that cache can store any response. |

Not guaranteed, by design:

- In a **shared** cache, a response stored for an anonymous request is served to authorized requests for the same URL
  too, and responses that depend on cookies are shared unless the origin sends `Vary: Cookie` or `private`. That is
  what RFC 9111 specifies for a shared cache. Add `Cookie` or `Authorization` to `KeyHeaders` when your origin
  personalises without saying so.
- Anonymous callers of a private cache are one caller: they share responses.
- Debug and warning logs include request URLs. Don't put secrets in query strings.

## MethodCache.OpenTelemetry

With the default options, nothing that identifies a person or an argument leaves the process:

| Signal | Recorded by default | Opt-in |
|---|---|---|
| Span attributes | method name, hit or miss, TTL, group, version, number of keys invalidated; on failure the exception type, message and stack trace | `RecordCacheKeys` (a SHA-256 hash of the key, or the key itself with `HashCacheKeys = false`); `RecordCacheTags` (tags and invalidation patterns, which contain argument values when built from templates) |
| Span baggage | the correlation and invalidation ids you set | `ExportSensitiveData` adds the user and tenant ids |
| Metrics | dimensions `method`, `group`, `version`, `error.type`, and `client` and `outcome` for HTTP caching | none: tags, keys and URLs are never metric dimensions |

Cache spans copy the `http.*` and `url.*` attributes of the request span they belong to; turn off
`EnableHttpCorrelation` if those hold data your traces shouldn't. Exception messages come from your own code; keep
personal data out of them.

## The tests

Each row above is pinned by a test: `AdminEndpointSecurityTests` (ASP.NET Core), `HttpCacheIsolationTests` and
`UntrustedEntryTests` (HTTP caching), `TelemetryDefaultsLeakTests` (OpenTelemetry), `KeyInjectionPropertyTests` and
`DistributedCacheSecurityTests` (keys, tags and the distributed cache).


Unknown HTTP transports (including opaque wrappers and native platform handlers) bypass caching by default and emit one warning per named client. Set `AllowUnverifiedTransport` only when you have verified that the whole transport sends no automatic cookies or hidden caller identity. Recognized transports with automatic cookies always bypass.

`AddHttpCaching()` disables automatic cookies on the named client’s `SocketsHttpHandler` or `HttpClientHandler`, after all primary-handler configuration. The default registration therefore caches immediately. Send caller cookies explicitly; a handler that manages a hidden cookie jar belongs on a client without HTTP caching. Other named clients are unaffected.

Backplane invalidations do not cross wire versions in either direction. Deploy the same MethodCache version on all nodes sharing a cache/backplane; a rolling upgrade needs a new cache namespace or a coordinated cache clear. New message type numbers prevent legacy keys from being mistaken for encoded frames. Rejected frames emit one warning per backplane instance without logging their contents.

`AddHttpCaching()` runs the cache after all additional handlers, so injected caller identity and rewritten requests are visible before lookup. Delegating handlers inside the primary transport, or below a directly constructed cache handler, are unverified and bypass caching unless the entire chain is explicitly trusted.


---

<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

To see what is actually cached, list the entries with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or `GET /methodcache/entries`,
and the effective policy of every method with `GetMethods()` or `GET /methodcache/methods` ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## The method runs on every call

- **The attribute is on the class.** `[Cache]` is read from the interface only. The analyzer reports
  [MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) and its code fix moves the attribute.
- **The service was registered after `AddMethodCache()`.** Call `AddMethodCache()` after your own registrations.
- **The caller doesn't use the interface.** The cache is a decorator around the interface. Resolving or injecting the
  class itself, or calling the method from inside the class (`this.GetAsync(...)`), skips it.
- **The arguments differ between calls.** A `DateTime.Now`, a new `Guid` or a request object with a unique id in it
  makes every key different. List the keys to check ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)).
- **The result is not stored on purpose:** a `CacheWhen` predicate rejected it, the result is `null` with
  `CacheNullValues = false`, or the call threw. Exceptions are never cached.
- **A test registered `NoOpCacheManager`**, which never caches ([Testing](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/testing.md)).

## Old data after an update

- **The tags don't match.** `[CacheInvalidate]` removes only the tags it lists. Compare them with the cached methods'
  tags.
- **A tag template isn't filled in.** The name in braces must be a parameter of that method:
  [MCG009](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg009) warns about unknown names. A property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is
  not a template and stays literal ([MCG015](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mcg015)); pass the id as a parameter.
- **The update method threw.** Invalidation runs only after the method completes successfully.
- **The data changed outside the interface**, for example in another service or a database job. Invalidate from that
  code with `ICacheManager.InvalidateByTagsAsync` ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md#from-code)).
- **You run several instances** with only the in-memory cache. Each instance has its own cache; add
  [Redis or SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md) so invalidations reach all of them. With a custom
  `IDistributedCache`, also register an `IBackplane`.
- **Fail-safe returned an expired value** because the method failed ([Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md)).

## A change in appsettings.json has no effect

- `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration(builder.Configuration)` must be called.
- The key under `Services` must be the method id: the interface's full name, a dot and the method name. An unknown id
  is logged as a warning at startup. `GET /methodcache/methods` lists the ids.
- A runtime override for the method wins over the file ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).
- An invalid value in a reloaded file is logged as an error, and the previous policies stay.

## Exceptions

| Exception | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `InvalidOperationException` when building a key | An argument type has only private state, so every value would get the same key. Implement `ICacheKeyProvider` ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#types-whose-state-is-private)) |
| `InvalidOperationException` at startup | `OnHit`, `OnMiss`, `WithMetrics` or `When` configured for a `[Cache]` method. They apply to `GetOrCreateAsync` only |
| `NotSupportedException` from `InvalidateByTagPatternAsync` | Pattern invalidation doesn't work with a distributed cache. Invalidate exact tags |
| `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `WithDuration` | Durations must be positive. An override can't turn caching off; invalidate instead |
| An exception from `AddMethodCacheFromConfiguration` | An invalid value in the `MethodCache` section at startup |

## A caller changed a cached object, and others see the change

The cache hands the same instance to every caller. Return immutable types such as records, or copies
([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md#cached-objects-are-shared)).

## Build errors and warnings

Every `MC` and `MCG` diagnostic, with what to do about it, is in [Build diagnostics](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md -->

# Build Diagnostics

MethodCache checks your attributes when you build. Errors mean the method would not be cached as written, so the
build stops; warnings point at attributes that do nothing. Every diagnostic links to its section below, and the ones
marked **Code fix** can be fixed from the light bulb in Visual Studio, Rider or VS Code.

| Id | Severity | Summary | Code fix |
|----|----------|---------|----------|
| [MC0001](#mc0001) | Warning | `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on a class member | Move to the interface |
| [MC0004](#mc0004) | Error | A time span that is not a positive `TimeSpan` | |
| [MCG001](#mcg001) | Error | `[Cache]` on a `void` method | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG002](#mcg002) | Error | `[Cache]` on `Task`/`ValueTask` without a result | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG003](#mcg003) | Error | `[Cache]` with reference parameters or returns | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG004](#mcg004) | Error | `[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method | |
| [MCG005](#mcg005) | Warning | `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags | |
| [MCG006](#mcg006) | Error | `[Cache]` with pointer or function pointer parameters or returns, including arrays of them | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG007](#mcg007) | Error | `[Cache]` with ref struct parameters or returns | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG009](#mcg009) | Warning | A tag names a parameter the method does not have | Use the closest parameter |
| [MCG010](#mcg010) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type it can't decorate | |
| [MCG011](#mcg011) | Error | `[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method it can't cache | |
| [MCG012](#mcg012) | Error | The same interface in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]` | |
| [MCG013](#mcg013) | Error | An interface with static or non-public abstract members | |
| [MCG014](#mcg014) | Error | `[Cache]` on a lazy sequence | Remove `[Cache]` |
| [MCG015](#mcg015) | Warning | A tag placeholder that is not a parameter name, such as `{product.Id}` | |
| [MCG016](#mcg016) | Warning | A tag placeholder matches several parameter names without an exact spelling match | |

## MC0001

`[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` is on a class, struct or record member. MethodCache generates a decorator for the
interface, so it only reads attributes on interface methods, and this one is ignored.

```csharp
public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00")]      // here
    Task<User> GetAsync(int id);
}

public class UserService : IUserService
{
    public Task<User> GetAsync(int id) => ...;   // not here
}
```

**Code fix:** moves the attribute to the interface method the member implements (adding the `using` if needed), or
removes it when the member implements no interface. To cache an interface you don't own, see the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MC0004

`Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `FailSafe` or `FailSafeTimeout` on `[Cache]` or
`[assembly: CacheInterface]` is not a positive time span. Use the `TimeSpan` format: `"00:05:00"` (five minutes),
`"01:00:00"` (an hour) or `"1.00:00:00"` (a day). `FailSafe` also accepts `"off"`.

## MCG001

`[Cache]` on a `void` method: there is no result to cache. Return the value, or remove `[Cache]`. If the method
changes data, you probably want `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MCG002

`[Cache]` on a method returning `Task` or `ValueTask` without a result. Return `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`, or remove
`[Cache]`. A write method usually wants `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` instead.

## MCG003

`[Cache]` on a method with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters, or a `ref` / `ref readonly` return.
A cached value cannot preserve references or set an `out` value. Pass and return values by value, for example as a record.

## MCG004

`[Cache]` and `[CacheInvalidate]` on the same method. A method either reads (cached) or writes (invalidates); keep
the one that matches what it does.

## MCG005

`[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing. List the tags of the cached methods it should clear:

```csharp
[Cache(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task<User> GetAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = new[] { "users", "user:{id}" })]
Task UpdateAsync(int id, User user);
```

## MCG006

`[Cache]` on a method with pointer or function pointer parameters or returns, including arrays of them such as
`int*[]`. These cannot be stored as cached values or keys; use a value or an array of values. Unsupported methods, and
any other member of the interface that uses a pointer, are still forwarded through an unsafe implementation.

## MCG007

`[Cache]` on a method with `Span<T>`, `ReadOnlySpan<T>` or other ref struct parameters or returns. These cannot be
stored in a cache; use an array, `Memory<T>` or a string.

## MCG009

A tag such as `"user:{userId}"` names a parameter the method does not have, so the braces stay literal text and every
call shares that tag. The name between the braces must match a parameter name (case doesn't matter).

A template takes a parameter name only; a property path such as `"{product.Id}"` is reported as [MCG015](#mcg015).

**Code fix:** offers the closest parameter names, so `"user:{usrId}"` becomes `"user:{userId}"`.

## MCG010

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` names a type MethodCache can't decorate: a class, a generic interface, an interface that
is not accessible, one with static abstract members, or one declared in your own project (put `[Cache]` on its methods
instead). It is also reported when the attribute lists no methods. See the [third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MCG011

`[assembly: CacheInterface]` lists a method that is missing, overloaded, or returns nothing to cache. Use
`nameof(IClient.Method)` so a rename is caught by the compiler. See the
[third-party caching page](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/third-party.md).

## MCG012

The same interface is listed in more than one `[assembly: CacheInterface]`. List each interface once, with all its
methods in the same attribute.

## MCG013

Nested helper type declarations are supported and do not count as abstract service members.

The interface has static abstract members, or non-public abstract members that cannot be forwarded to the decorated instance. Move the cached methods to an interface without them. Non-public default helpers are supported because they remain on the interface.

## MCG014

`[Cache]` on a method returning `IEnumerable<T>`, `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`. The cached value would be
the lazy sequence itself, which runs the query again on every enumeration. Return a materialized collection, such as
`Task<List<T>>`, `Task<IReadOnlyList<T>>` or `T[]`, and call `ToListAsync()` (or similar) in the implementation.

## MCG015

A tag has braces that look like a template but don't hold a plain parameter name: a property path such as
`"product:{product.Id}"`, spaces such as `"{ id }"`, or a format such as `"{day:yyyy-MM-dd}"`. Templates take a
parameter name only, so the braces stay literal text and every call shares the same tag. Write `"product:{id}"` and
add the value as its own parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md). For `[assembly: CacheInterface]` both MCG009 and MCG015 are reported on the
attribute.

## MCG016

The placeholder has no exact parameter match and more than one case-insensitive match, such as `{NAME}` for parameters `name` and `Name`. Use the intended parameter’s exact spelling. Until corrected, the placeholder remains literal in both cached tags and invalidation.


---

<!-- source: docs/migration-from-imemorycache.md -->

# Migrating from IMemoryCache

With `IMemoryCache`, every cached method holds the same pattern: build a key, try the cache, load, store, and remember
every key to remove when data changes. MethodCache moves that into an attribute on the interface.

<table>
<tr><th>Before: IMemoryCache</th><th>After: MethodCache</th></tr>
<tr><td>

```cs
public async Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id)
{
    var key = $"user:{id}";
    if (_cache.TryGetValue(key, out User? user))
        return user!;

    // Two callers can both miss and both hit the database
    user = await _db.LoadUserAsync(id);
    _cache.Set(key, user, TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));
    return user;
}

public async Task RenameAsync(int id, string name)
{
    await _db.RenameAsync(id, name);
    _cache.Remove($"user:{id}");
    // ...and every other key that held this user
}
```

</td><td>

```cs
[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task<User> GetUserAsync(int id);

[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["user:{id}"])]
Task RenameAsync(int id, string name);
```

</td></tr>
</table>

## Steps

1. Add the `MethodCache` package and call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` after your registrations
   ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)).
2. If the class has no interface, extract one. Callers must use the interface, because the cache is a decorator around
   it.
3. Move the caching settings to `[Cache]` on the interface method, and delete the cache code from the implementation.
4. Replace each `Remove(key)` with `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = ...)]` on the method that changes the data, and give the
   cached methods matching tags ([Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md)).
5. Code that can't move to an attribute, such as a cached call in the middle of a method, uses
   `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync` with the key it already has ([Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md)).

Migrate one service at a time; both caches can run side by side.

## What maps to what

| IMemoryCache | MethodCache |
|--------------|-------------|
| `TryGetValue` + `Set` | `[Cache]`, or `GetOrCreateAsync` with your key |
| `SetAbsoluteExpiration` | `Duration` |
| `SetSlidingExpiration` | `SlidingExpiration`, capped by `Duration` |
| `Remove(key)` | `[CacheInvalidate]` with tags, or `InvalidateByKeysAsync` |
| `Size` and `SizeLimit` | `Weigher` and `MaxMemoryBytes` ([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)) |
| `Priority` | Not needed: W-TinyLFU keeps the entries that are read often |
| `GetOrCreateAsync`, which may run the factory several times at once | Concurrent misses share one call |
| A separate `IDistributedCache` | `AddMethodCacheRedis(...)`, with the memory cache kept in sync ([Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md)) |

## Differences to know

- **Keys are generated** from the method and its arguments ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)). Check that every argument
  that changes the result is a parameter, not a field of the class.
- **`null` is cached** by default. Set `CacheNullValues = false` if your old code skipped `null`.
- **Exceptions are never cached**, as before.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.Redis/README.md -->

# MethodCache.Redis

Redis as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache over Redis pub/sub.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis(options =>
{
    options.Configuration = "redis1:6379,redis2:6379,password=...";
    options.KeyPrefix = "orders-api:";   // the backplane channel follows: orders-api:invalidations
});
```

MethodCache keeps its own cache and connection, so your app's `IDistributedCache` and Redis settings are left alone. The connection opens on first use, so the application starts while Redis is down. It uses `BacklogPolicy.FailFast`, so a cache miss runs your method instead of waiting for Redis.

To share a connection your app already has instead:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis(options =>
    options.ConnectionMultiplexerFactory = sp => sp.GetRequiredService<IConnectionMultiplexer>());
```

MethodCache doesn't dispose a shared connection; disposing the service provider only removes MethodCache's own
subscriptions (`DisposeAsync` waits for that).

## How it works

- Entries are stored through `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis`, so values are written without extra copies.
- Values are JSON written with System.Text.Json; add `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` and call `AddMethodCacheMessagePack()` for MessagePack. Each entry records its format, so after a switch older entries count as misses.
- MethodCache reads Redis on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Invalidating a key removes it from Redis. Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as missing, so no tag sets are kept in Redis.
- Invalidation times are stored atomically, so an older invalidation that arrives late never undoes a newer one. Upgrade every instance that shares a `KeyPrefix` together, since earlier builds don't.
- Both also publish a message, so every instance drops its in-memory copies at once.
- Pub/sub delivers nothing while a connection is down. When the connection comes back, the instance clears its in-memory cache and reads entries from Redis again.
- Pattern invalidation (`InvalidateByTagPatternAsync`) is not supported with a distributed cache and throws `NotSupportedException`.

## When Redis is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; Redis never fails or stalls a call.

- Every Redis call is capped at `OperationTimeout` (1 second).
- After a failure or timeout, MethodCache skips Redis for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds), then one call checks whether it is back. The first failure and the recovery are logged.
- Invalidations that Redis doesn't accept are queued and retried until it does. They never throw. Until they are stored, this instance doesn't read entries from Redis, so an invalidated value can't come back.
- A value set directly while Redis is down stays in this instance's memory; the value it replaced is removed from Redis and the other instances once Redis is back.
- `ClockSkewTolerance` (2 seconds) covers servers whose clocks differ: a tag invalidation also applies to entries created up to that long after it.

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<DistributedCacheOptions>(options =>
{
    options.OperationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
    options.CircuitBreakerDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
});
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `Configuration` | `localhost:6379` | StackExchange.Redis configuration string |
| `ConnectionMultiplexerFactory` | none | Returns an existing connection to share instead of opening one |
| `KeyPrefix` | `methodcache:` | Prefix for every key MethodCache writes |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Send invalidations to other instances over pub/sub |
| `BackplaneChannel` | `KeyPrefix` + `invalidations` | Pub/sub channel; applications with different key prefixes get different channels |

## Behavior and compatibility

Distributed tags and backplane keys/tags preserve exact UTF-16 code units, including lone surrogates. Envelope version 4 and backplane frames use lossless representations; older envelopes are cache misses. Deploy the same MethodCache version across nodes sharing a cache and backplane.

Redis escapes unpaired UTF-16 surrogates and backslashes in physical keys, keeping distinct logical keys separate in every data and invalidation operation. Ordinary keys and their prefixes stay unchanged.

Backplane invalidations do not cross wire versions in either direction. Deploy the same MethodCache version on all nodes sharing a cache/backplane; a rolling upgrade needs a new cache namespace or a coordinated cache clear. New message type numbers prevent legacy keys from being mistaken for encoded frames. Rejected frames emit one warning per backplane instance without logging their contents.


---

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.SqlServer/README.md -->

# MethodCache.SqlServer

SQL Server as MethodCache's distributed cache. Results are shared between application instances, and invalidations reach every instance's in-memory cache through a table that each instance polls.

## Usage

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheSqlServer(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Cache")!);
```

With options:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheSqlServer(options =>
{
    options.ConnectionString = connectionString;
    options.SchemaName = "cache";
    options.BackplanePollingInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
});
```

## Tables

By default the schema and two tables are created when the application starts, if they do not exist. Startup waits at most three seconds for that; if SQL Server is down, creation is retried in the background and methods run uncached until it succeeds.

- `MethodCache` holds the entries, in the layout `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.SqlServer` uses (the same as `dotnet sql-cache create`).
- `MethodCacheInvalidations` holds recent invalidations for the backplane. Applications that share it are kept
  apart by `KeyPrefix` (compared exactly, whatever the SQL collation).

If the application's login may not create tables, set `CreateTablesIfMissing = false` and create them in a migration instead.

### Upgrading from an earlier build

The invalidations table gets a nullable `Scope binary(32)` column and the indexes `Index_Scope_Id (Scope, Id)` and
`Index_Scope_CreatedAt (Scope, CreatedAt)`; with `CreateTablesIfMissing = false`, add them in your migration before
deploying. Rows without a scope are ignored, and each instance deletes them once they are older than its
`BackplaneRetention`, as the old build did. Cache entries
written by an earlier build become misses and expire normally. Upgrade every instance that shares the tables
together, and restart them with empty in-memory caches.

## How it works

- Entries are stored through MethodCache's own `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.SqlServer` cache, which also removes expired rows. Your app's `IDistributedCache` is left alone.
- Values are JSON written with System.Text.Json; add `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack` and call `AddMethodCacheMessagePack()` for MessagePack.
- MethodCache reads SQL Server on an in-memory miss and writes new results to both.
- Invalidation times are stored atomically, so an older invalidation that arrives late never undoes a newer one.
- Keys are stored hashed, so keys that SQL collation would treat as equal (casing, trailing spaces, Unicode forms) stay distinct. Keys and tags of any length get a fixed-size ID.
- Invalidating a key removes its row. Invalidating a tag stores the time of the invalidation, and entries with that tag written before it are treated as missing, so no tag tables are needed.
- Both also add a row to the invalidations table. Other instances read new rows every `BackplanePollingInterval` and drop their in-memory copies.
- A message that fails to apply is retried on the next poll. If it still fails after five polls, the instance clears its in-memory cache in its place and moves on, so one bad message can't hold back the ones after it.
- Each instance deletes its own prefix's rows older than its `BackplaneRetention` from the invalidations table, along with rows an earlier build wrote without a prefix. Rows of a prefix that no running application uses any more are never deleted; delete them by hand.
- Identity values are handed out before a transaction commits, so a row can appear after later ones were read. The ids an instance skipped are checked again for a few seconds; ids taken by other prefixes' rows in a shared table are recognized as committed and are not checked again.
- An instance that couldn't read the invalidations table for half of `BackplaneRetention` may have missed invalidations, so it clears its in-memory cache.
- Pattern invalidation (`InvalidateByTagPatternAsync`) is not supported with a distributed cache and throws `NotSupportedException`.

## When SQL Server is down

MethodCache keeps answering from memory and your methods; SQL Server never fails or stalls a call.

- Every SQL Server call is capped at `OperationTimeout` (1 second).
- After a failure or timeout, MethodCache skips SQL Server for `CircuitBreakerDuration` (10 seconds), then one call checks whether it is back. The first failure and the recovery are logged.
- Invalidations that SQL Server doesn't accept are queued and retried until it does. They never throw. Until they are stored, this instance doesn't read entries from SQL Server, so an invalidated value can't come back.
- A value set directly while SQL Server is down stays in this instance's memory; the value it replaced is removed from SQL Server and the other instances once SQL Server is back.
- `ClockSkewTolerance` (2 seconds) covers servers whose clocks differ: a tag invalidation also applies to entries created up to that long after it.

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<DistributedCacheOptions>(options =>
{
    options.OperationTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500);
    options.CircuitBreakerDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
});
```

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `ConnectionString` | (required) | SQL Server connection string |
| `SchemaName` | `dbo` | Schema of both tables |
| `TableName` | `MethodCache` | Table for cache entries |
| `InvalidationsTableName` | `MethodCacheInvalidations` | Table the backplane uses |
| `KeyPrefix` | `methodcache:` | Prefix for every key MethodCache writes; also keeps backplanes that share the tables apart |
| `CreateTablesIfMissing` | `true` | Create the schema and tables at startup |
| `EnableBackplane` | `true` | Share invalidations with other instances |
| `BackplanePollingInterval` | 1 second | How often each instance reads new invalidations |
| `BackplaneRetention` | 1 hour | How long invalidations are kept; at least one minute |

## Behavior and compatibility

Distributed tags and backplane keys/tags preserve exact UTF-16 code units, including lone surrogates. Envelope version 4 and backplane frames use lossless representations; older envelopes are cache misses. Deploy the same MethodCache version across nodes sharing a cache and backplane.

Backplane invalidations do not cross wire versions in either direction. Deploy the same MethodCache version on all nodes sharing a cache/backplane; a rolling upgrade needs a new cache namespace or a coordinated cache clear. New message type numbers prevent legacy keys from being mistaken for encoded frames. Rejected frames emit one warning per backplane instance without logging their contents.

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.AspNetCore/README.md -->

# MethodCache.AspNetCore

Admin endpoints and a health check for MethodCache's in-memory cache.

## Setup

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IUserService, UserService>();
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks().AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddAuthorization(o => o.AddPolicy("CacheAdmins", p => p.RequireRole("Admin")));

var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapMethodCacheAdmin("CacheAdmins");
app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
```

The authorization policy is required, because the endpoints expose cache keys and can empty the cache; a
signed-in user without the policy gets 403.

## Endpoints

All paths are relative to the prefix (`/methodcache` by default).

| Method | Path | What it does |
|--------|------|--------------|
| `GET` | `stats` | Hits, misses, hit ratio, evictions, entries and estimated memory |
| `GET` | `methods` | The effective policy of every cached method and where it came from |
| `GET` | `entries?prefix=&tag=&limit=` | Live entries ordered by key (default limit 100, max 1000). Values are not returned |
| `GET` | `entry?key=` | One entry, or 404 |
| `DELETE` | `entry?key=` | Removes one entry, or 404 |
| `POST` | `invalidate` | Removes entries by tag. Body: `{ "tags": ["users"] }` |
| `DELETE` | `entries` | Removes every entry |

The same operations are available in code through `ICacheAdministrator` in the `MethodCache` namespace.

## Health check

`AddMethodCache()` on the health checks builder reports Healthy when the cache answers, with `entries`,
`hitRatio`, `evictions` and `memoryUsageBytes` in the report data. With Redis or SQL Server it reports Degraded
while that cache is unreachable and MethodCache serves from memory only (`distributedCacheAvailable` in the data).
Each check asks the distributed cache once, waiting at most its operation timeout.

## Limits

- Works with the default in-memory cache manager. A custom `ICacheManager` has no `ICacheAdministrator`.
- Policies are read-only here. Change them at runtime with `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`.

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry/README.md -->

# MethodCache.OpenTelemetry

[![NuGet Version](https://img.shields.io/nuget/v/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry)](https://www.nuget.org/packages/MethodCache.OpenTelemetry)

OpenTelemetry metrics and traces for MethodCache.

The package depends only on the OpenTelemetry API, as instrumentation libraries should, so it works the same in
console apps, workers and ASP.NET Core. Your app brings the SDK and exporters. For request spans, add
`OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore` to your app as usual.

## What you get

- **Metrics for every call**:
  - hits, misses and errors per method;
  - how long the cached method took on a miss;
  - entries, memory and hit ratio of the in-memory cache.
- **Spans for misses and invalidations**:
  - Each span has the method, hit or miss, TTL, group and version. Keys and tags only when you turn them on, since they contain argument values.
  - Spans are children of the current request span and copy its `http.*` and `url.*` attributes.
- **Hits stay allocation-free**: generated decorators answer hits from the cache's fast path, which has no span. Hits still count in `methodcache.hits_total`.

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package MethodCache.OpenTelemetry
dotnet add package OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting   # the SDK and AddOpenTelemetry(), if your app doesn't have it yet
```

## Setup

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheOpenTelemetry(); // after AddMethodCache, which registers the cache it instruments

builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
    .WithTracing(tracing => tracing
        .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter())
    .WithMetrics(metrics => metrics
        .AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()
        .AddOtlpExporter());
```

Sampling, export intervals and the service name are set on the OpenTelemetry SDK as for any other library.

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `EnableTracing` | `true` | Creates spans |
| `EnableMetrics` | `true` | Records metrics |
| `RecordCacheKeys` | `false` | Puts the cache key on spans. Keys can contain argument values |
| `HashCacheKeys` | `true` | With `RecordCacheKeys`, records a hash of the key instead of the key |
| `RecordCacheTags` | `false` | Puts the cache tags and invalidation patterns on spans. Tags such as `user:{userId}` contain argument values |
| `ExportSensitiveData` | `false` | Puts the user and tenant ids from `IBaggagePropagator` into span baggage |
| `EnableHttpCorrelation` | `true` | Copies the request's `http.*` and `url.*` attributes onto cache spans |
| `EnableBaggagePropagation` | `true` | Carries `cache.*` baggage between spans |

## Baggage

`IBaggagePropagator` carries a correlation id, an invalidation id, a user id and a tenant id along the async flow,
and puts them into the baggage of cache spans, which travels to downstream services. The user and tenant ids
identify people, so they are left out unless `ExportSensitiveData` is on. A value set in a child task stays in that
task.

```cs
_baggagePropagator.SetCacheCorrelationId(Guid.NewGuid().ToString());
_baggagePropagator.SetCacheTenantId(tenantId); // exported only with ExportSensitiveData = true
```

## Span attributes

| Attribute | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `cache.method` | Method name | `IUserService.GetUserAsync` |
| `cache.hit` | Whether the value came from the cache | `true` |
| `cache.key` / `cache.key_hash` | The key, with `RecordCacheKeys` | `a1b2c3d4` |
| `cache.ttl_seconds` | Time-to-live | `600` |
| `cache.tags` | Cache tags, with `RecordCacheTags` | `user,profile` |
| `cache.group` | Group | `users` |
| `cache.version` | Version | `2` |
| `cache.keys_count` | Number of keys invalidated | `3` |

## Metrics

Metric dimensions are kept to values with few variants (`method`, `group`, `version`, `error.type`), so a tag such
as `user:42` never becomes a time series of its own.

| Metric | Type | Description | Dimensions |
|--------|------|-------------|------------|
| `methodcache.hits_total` | Counter | Cache hits, including fast-path hits | method |
| `methodcache.misses_total` | Counter | Cache misses | method |
| `methodcache.errors_total` | Counter | Errors (`load_failed` when the cached method throws) | method, error.type |
| `methodcache.load_duration` | Histogram (ms) | Time the cached method took on a miss or refresh | method |
| `methodcache.operation_duration` | Histogram (ms) | Duration of instrumented operations (misses, invalidations) | method, group, version |
| `methodcache.key_generation_duration` | Histogram (ms) | Key generation on instrumented operations | method |
| `methodcache.entries_count` | Gauge | Entries in the in-memory cache | |
| `methodcache.memory_bytes` | Gauge | Estimated memory of the in-memory cache | |
| `methodcache.hit_ratio` | Gauge | Hits / (hits + misses) | |

## Troubleshooting

**No spans.** Check that the SDK listens to the source with `.AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()` on the tracer
provider. `TracingConstants.ActivitySource.HasListeners()` is true once it does.

**No HTTP attributes on cache spans.** Cache spans copy them from the request span, so enable ASP.NET Core
instrumentation: `.WithTracing(t => t.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation().AddMethodCacheInstrumentation())`.

## License

MIT License - see LICENSE file for details.

## Behavior and compatibility

Tracing counts cached `null` values as hits, including nullable value types.

Tracing uses `ICacheManager.LookupAsync` to distinguish a cached null from a miss in one memory lookup, including disabled fast paths and refresh-ahead windows. Like `TryGetAsync`, it does not load from L2 or start a factory.

<!-- source: src/MethodCache.HttpCaching/README.md -->

# MethodCache.HttpCaching

HTTP caching for `HttpClient`, the way a browser does it: responses are cached according to `Cache-Control`,
revalidated with `ETag` / `Last-Modified`, and a `304 Not Modified` comes back to your code as the full cached
response. It follows RFC 9111.

```cs
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IGitHubClient, GitHubClient>()
    .AddHttpCaching();
```

That is all. Your typed client keeps calling `GetAsync` as before.

## What it does

| The server sends | What happens on the next request |
|---|---|
| `Cache-Control: max-age=60` | Served from cache for 60 seconds, no network call |
| `ETag: "abc"` (or `Last-Modified`) | Sent with `If-None-Match: "abc"`; a 304 is answered from the cache |
| both | Served from cache while fresh, then revalidated with the ETag |
| `Vary: Accept-Language` | One cached response per language |
| `no-store` | Never cached |

- A successful `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` removes the cached responses for that URL (and for same-origin
  `Location` / `Content-Location`) for every caller, language and key header value, so nobody reads stale data
  after a write.
- Cached responses carry an `Age` header, as the standard requires.
- `Set-Cookie` is never stored: the caller the server answered gets it, nobody served from the cache does.
- Each HttpClient has its own settings and its own entries.
- Request directives are honored: `no-cache` (revalidates and stores the answer), `no-store`, `max-age`, `max-stale`, `min-fresh` and `only-if-cached`.
- `Range` requests go to the origin, and `206 Partial Content` is never stored.
- Requests that carry their own `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since` go to the origin, so your `304` reaches you.
- Statuses that are cacheable by default (`200`, `203`, `204`, `301`, `404`, ...) are stored; other `2xx` responses only when they say how long they stay fresh (`max-age` or `Expires`).

## Settings

Settings are per HttpClient:

```cs
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IWeatherClient, WeatherClient>()
    .AddHttpCaching(options =>
    {
        options.EnableStaleIfError = true;           // serve the last response when the API is down
        options.EnableStaleWhileRevalidate = true;   // when the server sends stale-while-revalidate
        options.AddDiagnosticHeaders = true;         // X-Cache: HIT / MISS / REVALIDATED / STALE
    });
```

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `IsSharedCache` | `false` | `false`: a private cache; `Authorization` and `Cookie` are part of the key so callers never see each other's responses. `true`: a shared cache; `private` and authorized responses are not stored, `s-maxage` applies, and a response stored for an anonymous request is served to every caller (see [Security](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/security.md#methodcachehttpcaching)) |
| `DefaultMaxAge` | `null` | Freshness for a response with only an `ETag`/`Last-Modified`. `null` revalidates every time |
| `AllowHeuristicFreshness` | `true` | 10% of the time since `Last-Modified`, at most `MaxHeuristicFreshness` (1 hour) |
| `StaleRetention` | 24 hours | How long a stale entry is kept for revalidation and the stale options below |
| `EnableStaleWhileRevalidate` | `false` | Serve stale at once and refresh in the background, within the server's `stale-while-revalidate` |
| `EnableStaleIfError` | `false` | Serve stale when the request fails or returns 5xx, within `stale-if-error` or `MaxStaleIfError` (24 hours) |
| `MaxResponseSize` | 10 MB | Larger responses are not cached. A body without `Content-Length` is read up to this size, then streamed to the caller uncached |
| `KeyHeaders` | empty | Request headers that are always part of the key, for APIs that vary on a header without sending `Vary` |
| `CacheableMethods` | GET, HEAD | POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are never cached, even if added. |
| `AddDiagnosticHeaders` | `false` | Adds `X-Cache`, `X-Cache-Age` and `X-Cache-TTL` |

`no-cache` requires successful validation, including when stale-while-revalidate or stale-if-error is enabled.
A request with `no-cache` also requires validation and propagates origin errors. `must-revalidate` (and
`proxy-revalidate` / `s-maxage` in a shared cache) forbids serving stale responses.

A 304 also updates storage policy: `no-store`, `Vary: *` or shared-cache `private` removes the old response,
including during background revalidation. Omitted `Vary` keeps the original variant selection.

An in-flight GET or background revalidation that started before a successful write cannot publish a response
into the new cache generation, including across instances. Publication generations are separate from response
writers. The built-in store bounds this metadata to 4096 slots per storage prefix; a slot collision can cause an
additional cache miss for another URL. Generation records use maximum absolute expiration; if the backend
evicts one anyway, a fresh generation starts, so the loss only causes misses and never serves a response from
before the write. Read failures fall back to the origin; invalidation write failures propagate after
the origin write, which may already have succeeded. Custom storage implementations implement
`GetGenerationAsync` and `InvalidateAsync` with shared, unique generations. See [HTTP caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/http-caching.md).

Cacheable bodies with an accurate `Content-Length` of up to 1 MB use one owned array. Larger, unknown or
inaccurate lengths use pooled temporary storage plus the final array; a declared length never allocates more than
1 MB up front, and a HEAD response allocates nothing for the `Content-Length` it carries. An oversized body remains readable as a stream; dispose the
response to release its storage.

## Storage

Responses are kept in memory, in a cache of their own (your app's `IMemoryCache` is not touched). The total size
is shared by all clients:

```cs
builder.Services.Configure<HttpCacheStorageOptions>(o => o.MaxCacheSize = 50 * 1024 * 1024); // default 100 MB
```

### Sharing responses between instances

With several instances of your app, each one would otherwise fetch and revalidate on its own. Turn on
`UseDistributedCache` and responses use MethodCache's own distributed cache from `AddMethodCacheRedis` or
`AddMethodCacheSqlServer`. If neither is registered, they use the application's `IDistributedCache`. The
application cache registration stays unchanged. Responses are kept outside memory, with the same
Redis or SQL Server that MethodCache uses:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCacheRedis("localhost:6379");
builder.Services.Configure<HttpCacheStorageOptions>(o => o.UseDistributedCache = true);
```

Now an ETag fetched by one instance is revalidated (and usually answered with a 304) by all of them, and a POST
through one instance invalidates the cached GET for all of them. If the distributed cache is down, requests go
straight to the origin. Apps that share one Redis or SQL Server should each set their own `KeyPrefix`
(default `methodcache-http:`). `ClearAsync()` cannot clear a distributed cache; entries there expire on their own.

To store responses somewhere else entirely, register your own `IHttpCacheStorage` before `AddHttpCaching()`:

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IHttpCacheStorage>(new DictionaryHttpCacheStorage(TimeProvider.System));
builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IGitHubClient, GitHubClient>()
    .AddHttpCaching();
```

A custom storage must implement `GetGenerationAsync` and `InvalidateAsync`: a successful POST, PUT, PATCH or
DELETE now invalidates only through `InvalidateAsync` (it used to call `RemoveAsync`), so a storage that implements
it as a no-op keeps serving old responses after a write. A minimal correct storage:

```cs
public sealed class DictionaryHttpCacheStorage(TimeProvider time) : IHttpCacheStorage
{
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, (HttpCacheEntry Entry, DateTimeOffset Expires)> _entries = new();
    private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, string> _generations = new();

    // Responses are stored per generation. A missing generation (never set, cleared or lost) starts a new
    // unique one, never a value used before, so losing it can only cause cache misses.
    public ValueTask<string> GetGenerationAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => ValueTask.FromResult(_generations.GetOrAdd(key, _ => Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")));

    // Called after a successful POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE: a fresh generation hides every older response.
    public ValueTask InvalidateAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _generations[key] = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public ValueTask<HttpCacheEntry?> GetAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => ValueTask.FromResult(_entries.TryGetValue(key, out var stored) && stored.Expires > time.GetUtcNow() ? stored.Entry : null);

    public ValueTask SetAsync(string key, HttpCacheEntry entry, TimeSpan timeToLive, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _entries[key] = (entry, time.GetUtcNow() + timeToLive);
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public ValueTask RemoveAsync(string key, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _entries.TryRemove(key, out _);
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public ValueTask ClearAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        _generations.Clear(); // in-flight requests can then only publish into orphaned generations
        _entries.Clear();
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }
}
```

### Time

Freshness, eviction from the memory store and the background revalidation timeout all read the time from the
`TimeProvider` registered in the container, if there is one. Register a fake `TimeProvider`, for example from
`Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`, to test expiry without waiting.

## Metrics

Every request is counted on the `MethodCache` meter, so `AddMethodCacheInstrumentation()` from
MethodCache.OpenTelemetry (or `AddMeter("MethodCache")`) picks them up:

| Instrument | Tags |
|---|---|
| `methodcache.http.requests_total` | `client`, `outcome` (`hit`, `miss`, `revalidated`, `stale`, `bypass`, `error` when the request threw) |
| `methodcache.http.request_duration` (ms) | `client`, `outcome` |

## Behavior and compatibility

A failed response-body read fails the request rather than returning a partially consumed body. Buffered and streamed responses release their original content resources on completion, cancellation or disposal.

`only-if-cached` never contacts the origin, including range requests, caller validators, `no-store`, unsupported methods and background revalidation. An unavailable representation returns 504.

HTTP cache keys preserve individual header-value boundaries, including `Cookie` and custom tenant headers.

An explicit `Expires` at or before the response date is stale immediately; heuristic freshness and `DefaultMaxAge` do not extend it.

An invalid `Expires` date (including `Expires: 0`) is immediately stale, even when heuristic freshness or a default lifetime is enabled. Explicit `max-age` and `s-maxage` take precedence.


Unknown HTTP transports (including opaque wrappers and native platform handlers) bypass caching by default and emit one warning per named client. Set `AllowUnverifiedTransport` only when you have verified that the whole transport sends no automatic cookies or hidden caller identity. Recognized transports with automatic cookies always bypass.

`AddHttpCaching()` disables automatic cookies on the named client’s `SocketsHttpHandler` or `HttpClientHandler`, after all primary-handler configuration. The default registration therefore caches immediately. Send caller cookies explicitly; a handler that manages a hidden cookie jar belongs on a client without HTTP caching. Other named clients are unaffected.

Oversized HTTP responses remain streamed; disposing them closes both stream segments and the original content owner, even if a custom owner does not close its stream.

HTTP key framing changes all response cache keys, including requests without `Vary`; old entries become cold misses. See the [release compatibility notes](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/developer/RELEASE_NOTES.md).

`AddHttpCaching()` runs the cache after all additional handlers, so injected caller identity and rewritten requests are visible before lookup. Delegating handlers inside the primary transport, or below a directly constructed cache handler, are unverified and bypass caching unless the entire chain is explicitly trusted.


---

<!-- source: docs/developer/RELEASE_NOTES.md -->

# Release compatibility notes

These changes are being made before the first nuget.org release.

## HTTP cache key format

Length framing changes **every HTTP response cache key**, including requests without `Vary` headers. Existing entries created by an older build will be cold misses after upgrading; the new build does not reuse them. This affects built-in and custom HTTP cache storage. Let old entries expire or clear their storage namespace during deployment.

## Distributed invalidation format

Backplane key and tag messages use new message types and lossless UTF-16 encoding. Invalidations do not cross between old and new wire versions in either direction. Upgrade every node sharing a cache and backplane together, with a coordinated cache clear, or use a new cache namespace. Old distributed envelopes are cache misses.
